summary: D. N. Dimri worked in indology and history and archaeology. A doctoral scholar at Doon University in 2014, Dimri served at UEEC, interned at WWF-India, was Director (Publications) at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2016), and researched at the University of Pannonia.
D. N. Shukla was an indologist who earned a D.Litt. from the University of Lucknow under K. A. Subramania Iyer. He was affiliated with Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1958).

D. Neil Schmid specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and completed doctoral studies at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair.
D. R. Nagaraj (1954–1998) worked in indology and other fields. He studied at Bangalore University, where he also held a post, and taught Sheldon Pollock.
D. S. Subbaramaiya was an indologist and philosopher who studied under traditional teachers Mallikere Subrahmanya Sastri and V. S. Ramachandra Sastri.
D. Srinivasachar was an indologist who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore, both attested from 1931 to 1933.
D. Venkat Rao specializes in indology, philosophy, and other fields, and held positions at the English and Foreign Languages University (attested 2003–2004 and 2014).

Dagfinn Føllesdal (1932–2026) studied at the University of Oslo and earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under W. V. O. Quine. Working in philosophy and linguistics, he taught at Harvard, Stanford University (1968–2011), and the University of Oslo.

Dagmar Schwerk specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her M.A. and Ph.D. under Dorji Wangchuk at the University of Hamburg, was a postdoctoral fellow at the University of British Columbia (2018–2022), and became a professor at the University of Leipzig in 2024.

Dagmar Wujastyk is an indologist and historian/archaeologist. She served as Principal Investigator at the University of Vienna in 2015 and became an Associate Professor at the University of Alberta in 2018.

Dagpo Rinpoche (born 1932) is an expert in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and taught David Seyfort Ruegg, Anne-Marie Blondeau, Thoupten Phuntshog, and Marie-Stella Boussemart.

Taichi Tado works in Buddhist studies and indology. Tado held teaching positions at Waseda University (attested 2020), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2020–2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Daiei Kaneko (1881–1976) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University. Kaneko founded Koho Gakuen and held posts at Toyo University (~1926–1928) and Otani University (~1928–1951).
Daigo Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2006).

Daijaku Judith Kinst specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She served on the faculty at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2013) and as Professor Emerita at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).
Daiju Sasaki (born 1977) is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Taisho University. He has taught at Taisho University (attested 2015 and 2026) and at Chisan Denpōin (attested 2015).

Daijō Tokiwa (1870–1945) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, and founded the Koa Buddhist Culture Research Institute.

Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Eihei-ji, and under Daicho Hayashi and Eko Hashimoto. He served at Zenshuji Soto Mission and San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and Hokyoji.

D. T. Suzuki (1870–1966) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Gakushuin, Otani, and Columbia, and founded the Eastern Buddhist Society and Matsugaoka Bunko.

Daishun Ueyama (1934–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as an associate professor, professor, and university president.
